entities.name: House of Bourbon
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The House of Bourbon, a cadet branch of the Capetian dynasty that rose to ruling prominence when Henry IV (Henry of Navarre) united the French crown and his Bourbon inheritance in 1589 following the Wars of Religion, subsequently produced the longest-ruling royal house of France (1589-1792, 1814-1830), the royal family of Spain (from Philip V, 1700-present, making it Europe's longest-continuing royal dynasty), and the royal families of Naples, Two Sicilies, Parma, and Luxembourg — making the Bourbons the most widely distributed royal house in European history.

The French Bourbons' defining moments: Henry IV's Edict of Nantes (1598) granting religious toleration to Huguenots — ending 36 years of religious civil war; Louis XIV (the Sun King, r. 1643-1715) — the epitome of European absolute monarchy, building Versailles as the model for European courts, reorganizing France's entire administrative system, and centralizing power so thoroughly he reportedly said 'L'état, c'est moi' ('I am the state'); Louis XVI's 1789 execution — the most consequential royal execution in modern history, inaugurating the French Revolutionary period.

The Spanish Bourbons (since Philip V, 1700) transformed Spain into a more centralized state following the War of the Spanish Succession (1701-1714). The current King of Spain Felipe VI (b. 1968) continues the Bourbon line, making Spain's royal family the last surviving European Bourbon monarchy and the only royal house founded after a major European war (War of Spanish Succession) still ruling its original kingdom.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The House of Bourbon — producing Louis XIV's model absolutism, Henry IV's religious toleration, Louis XVI's revolutionary execution, and continuing today in Spain — is the most widely distributed royal house in European history and the only one whose founding dynasty (1700) still rules its original kingdom, making it a unique bridge between early modern and contemporary European history.
